rv.q: It’s been a tough few years, though, and “Villette” is a modest and uneven production that has its moments but doesn’t fully capture the vivacity and lyrical intensity of my favorite of Brontë's novels, published six years after the far more famous “Jane Eyre.”
In all, it’s an alternately frustrating and engaging production.
VILLETTE is a classic drama that creates an intricate social world with strong performances.
Yu Shibagaki's set, consisting of overlapping wall panels the actors have to move, mostly gets in the way.
Based on a novel more people should read, “Villette” is a show worth seeing.
The last half of the play moves along rather slowly; the running time of almost 2.5 hours could be accelerated a bit.
The play was nearly perfect from my perspective, from the exceptional cast to the richly designed costumes to the haunting and moving set design and lighting.
It is a delightful two hours of theater and shows the versatility of Lookingglass Theatre Company.
